author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-09-19 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: How do I know that I am he?
context_before: How do I know this? Because I have awakened from the dream of life. I know that God laid himself down within me to sleep, to dream that he is I; for when he awoke, I was he!
context_after: Because his only begotten son, David, called me father.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Behold The Dreamer (1969-09-19).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-09-19 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: You and I are really one.
context_before: When God awakes within you he is the same God who awoke within me. There aren’t two Gods.
context_after: Although there appears to be billions of us here, we are all one being, one God acting out this play, to expand our creative power and wisdom.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Behold The Dreamer (1969-09-19).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-09-19 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Then I said to him, “Go and love.
context_before: Not long ago I was in another section of time instructing a group of maybe a dozen men all seated around me. In the center with me was a spectrum, a shadow of a man. I could move him about and do with him as I willed.
context_after: To the degree that you love, you will acquire substance. Only then can you take part in the drama and awake with life in yourself.”
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Behold The Dreamer (1969-09-19).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-09-19 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Joseph then saved civilization from starvation.
context_before: Now in the story, when Joseph joined his brothers, they said to one another: “Let us kill him.” But his brother, Judah pleaded for his life, saying: “No, he is our flesh and blood. Do not let his blood be upon us. Let us sell him into slavery.” So they stripped him of his robe and threw him into a pit. Then a caravan, on its way to Egypt carrying gold, incense, and myrrh (the same things the kings brought to the Christ child at his birth) agreed to buy him; and Joseph was taken into Egypt, where he rose to the power of Pharaoh.
context_after: And when the brothers were sorry for what they had done, Joseph said: “You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good.” Then his name was changed from Joseph to Joshua, which means Jesus.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Behold The Dreamer (1969-09-19).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-09-19 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: His history is divine, not secular.
context_before: The New Testament is all about the dreamer in you who awakens as Jesus Christ, and everything said of him is true.
